name: Repeated failed logons from one external address, then a success on the same account
description: Lab rule for the CTIA brute-force-001 scenario. One external IP produced a run of failed authentication events against a single account, and then that same address produced a successful logon for that same account. That is the shape of a credential brute force that has broken through, which is why the rule is written to catch both halves in one result set rather than only the failures: the alert is not interesting until you can see the success in the middle of it. The query is the same one the investigation uses, so the count the alert reports and the count you find by hand are the same number. Scoped to the alerting address on purpose so the result is unambiguous, and left without a threshold so every one of the records arrives as its own alert. The time window is deliberately long because this lab ships historical data - that is a lab-only concession, not a production setting; a real deployment would use a short window and alert on the shape of the burst rather than on a single address.
